source.title: Neuron Coverage-Guided Domain Generalization
source.authors: Chris Xing Tian; Haoliang Li; Xiao-Fei Xie; Yang Liu; Shi-Qi Wang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies neuron-coverage-guided domain generalization, not the prevalence or explanatory fidelity of neuron jobs named by a person. Its network-dissection examples describe individual visual units but do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports domain-generalization performance and ablations for its own neuron-coverage training method; these do not measure the claim's named-job proportions or test its versions, so they are not rows. It also reports qualitative network-dissection observations for individual ResNet-18 units; these are recorded below as findings about neurons that fit none of the versions.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a neuron-coverage training method for domain generalization and reports its accuracy. Its only neuron-interpretation content is a qualitative network-dissection look at two hand-picked ResNet-18 units, used to motivate the method. It gives no share of interpretable neurons, no test of explanations against where units fire, no automated scoring, and no neuron-level circuits. It tests none of V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that neuron-coverage maximization with gradient-similarity regularization improves domain generalization across benchmarks. The dissection visualizations are offered as support for that motivation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains vision models using neuron-coverage maximization and gradient-similarity regularization; it does not use the neuron-explanation audit or scoring methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that performance varies with which ResNet-18 layer outputs are included for coverage measurement and with parameter settings; it states that extreme parameter values can reduce performance.

fits_no_version.finding: In Sketch-trained ResNet-18 on PACS, the authors report that block 3 unit 170 shows an 'eye' concept under NCDG training but no semantic information under DeepAll. The images are hand-picked.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A training objective (neuron-coverage maximization) can change whether a selected unit shows a recognizable concept under network dissection.

fits_no_version.finding: Block 2 unit 20 shows edge and contour information under NCDG, while little useful information was observed under DeepAll.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For one selected low-level unit, the training method qualitatively changed the visual information seen by network dissection.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The neuron-interpretation evidence consists of qualitative visualizations of two selected units in one ResNet-18 setting; it does not report an interpretable-unit rate or a quantitative test of explanations.
record.rows_left_out: Domain-generalization accuracy tables, component ablations, and parameter analyses were omitted because they measure the performance of the paper's training method, not the claim's neuron-job interpretations.

record.verdict_notes: Changed the relation from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper never engages the claim, and only applies network dissection (Bau et al.) as a visualization tool. The dissection evidence is two cherry-picked units in one setting. No verdicts are given.

rows.subject: Resnet-18
rows.measure: Whether unit 170 shows an identifiable semantic concept on selected target-domain person images
rows.value: The authors report that they did not observe semantic information in unit 170 for DeepAll.
rows.note: The paper describes the result across selected images from the target domains; it does not give separate numerical results by domain.
rows.check: Qualitative illustration of one selected unit on hand-picked misclassified images. It is motivation for the method, not a measurement bearing on any version. Baseline 'NCDG model comparison' is a comparison of the study's own method, not a control.

rows.subject: Resnet-18
rows.measure: Whether unit 170 shows an identifiable semantic concept on selected target-domain person images
rows.value: The authors report that the concept of an eye was consistently extracted across samples.
rows.note: The paper says the selected images were misclassified by DeepAll and correctly classified by NCDG; it does not report a proportion of interpretable units.
rows.check: Same issue as R1. The 'eye' concept is shown on two images per domain chosen because NCDG classified them correctly, so the selection is in the method's favour.

rows.subject: Resnet-18
rows.measure: Whether the unit visualization shows useful visual information
rows.value: The authors report that useful information was difficult to observe in the DeepAll visualization.
rows.note: The paper gives a qualitative description rather than domain- or category-specific measurements.
rows.check: Qualitative illustration of one selected unit, used to motivate the method. It gives no rate of interpretable units.

rows.subject: Resnet-18
rows.measure: Whether the unit visualization shows useful visual information
rows.value: The authors report that the visualization showed some edge and contour information.
rows.note: The result is qualitative and does not estimate how many units have one identifiable job.
rows.check: Qualitative illustration of one selected unit, used to motivate the method. It gives no rate of interpretable units.
